question: At his hearing on 5 November 2024, the Commissioner for Democracy, Justice and the Rule of Law replied to a question on the primacy of EU law saying that ‘national courts are also EU courts’. 1.
Can the Commissioner comment further on this?
Does the Commission regard national courts and tribunals as mere implementers of EU legislation and case-law which is intended to protect the EU legal order from the national legal orders?
Does the Commission believe that national legal orders exist alongside – and not merely beneath – the EU legal order?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.2.2025) In line with the provisions of Article 19(1) of the Treaty on European Union and Article 267 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU, national courts and tribunals, in collaboration with the Court of Justice of the European Union, are entrusted with the interpretation and application of EU law1.

As such, national courts and tribunals act in a double capacity, as national and as EU courts. The national and EU legal systems form a common legal order2, providing EU citizens with complete and effective legal protection.
1 See, inter alia, Court of Justice of the European Union, judgment of 24 June 2019, case C-619/18,

ECLI:EU:C:2019:531, Commission v Poland, para. 71. 2 Court of Justice of the European Union, judgment of 16 February 2022, case C-156/21, Hungary v Parliament and Council, ECLI:EU:C:2022:97, para. 127.
